subs.label: Drama Series
subs.axis: Axis: by the dramatic premise that drives the series, from home and the self (prestige, family, everyday life, social realism, identity, youth, romance) through the professions and institutions (medicine, law, politics, work, music, sport, the military) to history and genre (war, Western, historical, costume, heritage, period, adventure, disaster), then the real and the formal (docudrama, biography, literary adaptation, anthology).

leaves.label: Prestige Drama
leaves.defn: A long-arc auteur drama whose engine is a morally compromised protagonist or a family/institution observed with novelistic ambition, made under the post-2000 cable "quality TV" banner (Mad Men, Six Feet Under, Billions, The Leftovers). A prestige crime saga goes to B7; a prestige family-business saga with succession at its centre goes to B1-3.
leaves.see: B1-3 Family Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Family Saga
leaves.defn: A serial that follows one family (or a few linked families) across generations or decades, so that historical time is the plot (Roots, Heimat, Pachinko, When Life Gives You Tangerines). A family drama set in one present moment goes to B1-3; a dynasty soap of wealth and scheming goes to B12-5.
leaves.see: B1-3 Family Drama; B1-22 Period Drama; B12-5 Prime-Time Soap Opera

leaves.label: Family Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the everyday bonds, conflicts and crises of one household or kin group in roughly its own present (Parenthood, This Is Us, The Waltons, Succession). A family followed across generations goes to B1-2; a family-revenge melodrama of the prime-time kind goes to B12-5.
leaves.aliases: domestic drama; family drama series; weekend drama (jumal deurama)
leaves.see: B1-2 Family Saga; B12-5 Prime-Time Soap Opera; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by what the family drama turns on, ensemble household first, then setting, wealth and marriage, the long broadcast family serial last

leaves.label: Slice-of-Life Drama
leaves.defn: A low-plot drama of ordinary lives, friendships and recoveries in which the texture of daily living, not an event, carries the series (thirtysomething, My Mister, Ode to Joy, Dear My Friends). Social-problem realism goes to B1-5; a romance-driven series goes to B1-9.
leaves.aliases: healing drama (hilling deurama); urban drama (dushi ju); ensemble drama
leaves.see: B1-5 Social Realist Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama; C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime
leaves.axis: by whose daily life is observed: friends and young adults, the wounded and healing, women in the city, then older people and whole communities

leaves.label: Social Realist Drama
leaves.defn: A drama that renders a social condition (class, work, abuse, faith, migration) with documentary-leaning realism and makes that condition the subject (Boys from the Blackstuff, This Is England '86, I May Destroy You, Unorthodox). A dramatisation of a real public case goes to B1-26.
leaves.aliases: kitchen sink realism; social problem drama; issue drama
leaves.see: B1-4 Slice-of-Life Drama; B1-26 Docudrama; B1-29 Anthology Drama
leaves.axis: by the social condition examined: working-class and community life, personal trauma and social issues, faith communities, migrants last

leaves.label: LGBTQ Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose central lives, community and conflicts are those of gay, lesbian, bisexual or trans characters (Queer as Folk, The L Word, POSE, It's a Sin). A teen coming-out romance stays in B1-7; East and Southeast Asian BL/GL series go to B5.
leaves.aliases: queer television; gay drama; lesbian drama
leaves.see: B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama; B1-7 Teen Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama

leaves.label: Teen Drama
leaves.defn: A drama centred on adolescents of secondary-school age and their school, friendships, first loves and coming of age (Beverly Hills, 90210, Degrassi, Skins, Euphoria). College and exam-coaching students go to B1-8; children's series for under-twelves go to B10.
leaves.aliases: high-school drama; teen soap; school drama (hakgyo deurama); seishun drama
leaves.see: B1-8 Campus Drama; B10 Children's Series; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by the teen engine: the glossy teen soap first, then issue drama, the school and its teachers, performing-arts schools, school violence, teen romance last

leaves.label: Campus Drama
leaves.defn: A drama of university students or exam aspirants in which the college or coaching institution is the world of the series (Felicity, Kota Factory, Aspirants, Hellcats). Secondary-school life goes to B1-7.
leaves.aliases: college drama; university drama; coaching-centre drama
leaves.see: B1-7 Teen Drama; B1-4 Slice-of-Life Drama

leaves.label: Romantic Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose main engine is a love story or the course of a relationship, played for feeling rather than laughs (Normal People, Virgin River, The Affair, Little Birds). A romantic comedy series goes to B8; a period romance in costume goes to B1-20; erotic film goes to A15.
leaves.aliases: romance series; love story; erotic drama
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B8 Comedy Series; A15 Erotic Film
leaves.axis: by the romantic engine: contemporary love story first, literary and young-adult romance, small-town romance, then the affair and the frankly erotic last

leaves.label: Medical Drama
leaves.defn: A series set among doctors, nurses and patients in which treating illness and the life of the hospital or practice drive the episodes (ER, Grey's Anatomy, House, Doctor X). A medical-crime investigation goes to B7.
leaves.see: B1-13 Workplace Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by where the medicine happens and who practises it: the hospital ensemble first, star doctors, emergency medicine, country doctors, nurses and allied staff, period medicine last

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A series in which lawyers, prosecutors, judges or juries and their cases are the engine (L.A. Law, The Good Wife, Suits, Extraordinary Attorney Woo). A police procedural goes to B7; a courtroom docudrama goes to B1-26.
leaves.aliases: courtroom drama; lawyer drama; hōtei drama
leaves.see: B7 Crime & Thriller Series; B1-26 Docudrama
leaves.axis: by which side of the law carries the series: the firm, the defence case, the prosecutor, the bench and jury, then comic and thriller treatments

leaves.label: Political Drama
leaves.defn: A series about the getting and use of political power by presidents, ministers, legislators and their staffs (The West Wing, Borgen, House of Cards, The Diplomat). An espionage thriller goes to B7; a dramatised real scandal goes to B1-26.
leaves.see: B1-26 Docudrama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the seat of power: head of state and executive first, parliament and party, city and campaign politics, diplomacy and the security state last

leaves.label: Workplace Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the work and rivalries of one non-medical, non-legal profession or company (The Newsroom, Chicago Fire, Misaeng: Incomplete Life, The Bear). Hospitals go to B1-10, law to B1-11, the military to B1-16; a workplace sitcom goes to B8.
leaves.aliases: professional drama; office drama (opisu deurama); procedural drama
leaves.see: B1-10 Medical Drama; B1-11 Legal Drama; B8 Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by the trade: newsrooms and media, first responders, offices and business, kitchens and hotels and trades, show business, then the caring professions

leaves.label: Musical Drama Series
leaves.defn: A drama whose world is the making of music or dance performance, with performances carrying story and feeling (Nashville, Smash, Daisy Jones & the Six, The Singing Detective). A performing-arts high school goes to B1-7; a music competition show goes to B13.
leaves.aliases: backstage musical; music drama; music-industry drama
leaves.see: B1-7 Teen Drama; A14 Musical & Dance Film; B13 Competition Formats

leaves.label: Sports Drama
leaves.defn: A series in which training for and competing in a sport or game is the spine of the story (Friday Night Lights, Cobra Kai, Racket Boys, Hikaru no Go). Sports anime goes to C7; live sport goes to B16.
leaves.see: C7 Sports & Game Anime; B16 Live Event & Sports Television
leaves.axis: by the kind of contest: team sports first, combat sports, individual and racing sports, mind sports and esports last

leaves.label: Military Drama
leaves.defn: A series about serving soldiers, sailors or special forces and their units in peacetime or present-day deployments, where service life is the engine (SEAL Team, The Unit, Sea Patrol, D.P.). A historical war goes to B1-17.
leaves.see: B1-17 War Drama; B1-13 Workplace Drama

leaves.label: War Drama
leaves.defn: A series set inside a historical war, on the front or behind it, in which the war itself drives the story (Band of Brothers, Das Boot, Generation War, Tour of Duty). Present-day service life goes to B1-16; war film goes to A9.
leaves.see: B1-16 Military Drama; A9 War Film; B1-22 Period Drama
leaves.axis: by the war, the Second World War first, then earlier wars, partisan and resistance cycles, later wars, home fronts and war nursing last

leaves.label: Television Western
leaves.defn: A series set on the American (or a comparable) frontier whose codes of gun, horse, land and law shape the story (Gunsmoke, Bonanza, Deadwood, Yellowstone). Western film goes to A10.
leaves.see: A10 Western; B1-2 Family Saga
leaves.axis: by kind of Western: the classic episodic Western first, frontier and pioneer drama, epic miniseries, the revisionist Western, the neo-Western last

leaves.label: Historical Drama
leaves.defn: A series that dramatises the great events and rulers of a pre-twentieth-century age, its wars, courts and faiths (I, Claudius, The Tudors, Vikings, The Crown). Ottoman historical dizi go to B12-6; Chinese and Korean court drama go to B4 and B2; a novel adaptation in period dress goes to B1-20.
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B12-6 Dizi; B4 Chinese-Language Drama; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by age and power: the ancient world first, biblical and religious epics, medieval and Renaissance, royal courts, colonial and slavery-era America, national and imperial epics last

leaves.label: Costume Drama
leaves.defn: A series adapted from (or modelled on) a pre-1900 novel, whose period manners, marriages and class are the drama (Pride and Prejudice, Bleak House, Anne of Green Gables, Bridgerton). Real rulers and battles go to B1-19; Edwardian country-house and shop sagas go to B1-21.
leaves.aliases: classic serial; period adaptation; bonnet drama
leaves.see: B1-19 Historical Drama; B1-21 Heritage Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama
leaves.axis: by literary source, Austen and the Regency first, the Victorian novel, continental classics, gothic and sensation fiction, classic girls' and school stories, then original costume romance

leaves.label: Heritage Drama
leaves.defn: A series that lovingly recreates late-Victorian to interwar British (and kindred) society through a great house, shop or village and the classes inside it (Upstairs, Downstairs, Downton Abbey, Mr Selfridge, The Jewel in the Crown). Novel adaptations of the 19th century go to B1-20.
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B1-22 Period Drama
leaves.axis: by the institution that holds the classes together: the country house, the shop or hotel, the village, then empire and Raj

leaves.label: Period Drama
leaves.defn: A series set in a recent past of the twentieth century (roughly 1918–1999) whose era, its manners and its changes are the drama (Pan Am, The Queen's Gambit, Cable Girls, Blossoms Shanghai). A series set within a war goes to B1-17; a multi-generation chronicle goes to B1-2.
leaves.aliases: period piece; era drama (niandai ju); nostalgia drama
leaves.see: B1-2 Family Saga; B1-17 War Drama; B1-21 Heritage Drama
leaves.axis: by decade, earliest first: interwar, the 1940s, the postwar and 1950s, the 1960s–70s, the 1980s–90s

leaves.label: Swashbuckler
leaves.defn: An episodic or serial adventure of swordplay, outlaw heroes, musketeers and pirates in a romanticised past (The Adventures of Robin Hood, Zorro, The Musketeers, Black Sails). Grounded medieval epics go to B1-19; martial-arts adventure goes to A7.
leaves.see: B1-19 Historical Drama; B1-24 Action-Adventure; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Action-Adventure
leaves.defn: A series built on quests, voyages, treasure hunts or a weekly hero-in-action format (Knight Rider, MacGyver, The Lost Tomb, Michael Strogoff). Swordplay romances go to B1-23; spy and crime action go to B7; superpowered heroes go to B9.
leaves.see: B1-23 Swashbuckler; B7 Crime & Thriller Series; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the adventure engine: literary adventure and voyages first, treasure hunts and tomb raiding, the weekly action hero, martial arts and street fighting last

leaves.label: Disaster Miniseries
leaves.defn: A miniseries whose story is an earthquake, eruption, impact or shipwreck and the struggle to survive it (10.5, Category 7: The End of the World, La Palma, Titanic). A dramatisation of a specific real disaster told as public record goes to B1-26.
leaves.see: B1-26 Docudrama; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Docudrama
leaves.defn: A drama that reconstructs a real event, case or institution with documentary fidelity, often naming the real people (Chernobyl, When They See Us, Mr Bates vs The Post Office, Dopesick). A dramatised life story goes to B1-27; a documentary series goes to B11.
leaves.see: B1-27 Biographical Miniseries; B11 Documentary Series; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the kind of real event: reenactment-led docudrama first, disasters, political scandal, injustice cases, terror and siege, corporate and public-health scandal, exploration and science last

leaves.label: Biographical Miniseries
leaves.defn: A miniseries or series that tells the life (or a defining stretch of it) of a real modern person (Fosse/Verdon, Elvis, Genius, The Kennedys). A pre-modern ruler goes to B1-19; biographical film goes to A11.
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; B1-26 Docudrama; B1-19 Historical Drama
leaves.axis: by the sphere of the life: politics and royalty first, musicians, show business and fashion, sport, then science, enterprise and faith

leaves.label: Literary Adaptation
leaves.defn: A limited series adapted from a modern literary novel or story, set in its author's present, where the book's voice shapes the drama (Olive Kitteridge, My Brilliant Friend, Patrick Melrose, The Slap). Pre-1900 novels go to B1-20; a literary romance goes to B1-9.
leaves.aliases: limited series; literary miniseries; prestige adaptation
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama; B1-1 Prestige Drama

leaves.label: Anthology Drama
leaves.defn: A series of self-contained plays or stories with new casts and stories per episode or season (Play for Today, Playhouse 90, Alfred Hitchcock Presents, Modern Love). Horror anthologies of the uncanny go to B9 when the supernatural is the engine.
leaves.aliases: anthology series; single play; omnibus drama
leaves.see: B9 Speculative Series; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the anthology unit: the live and single play first, suspense and crime tales, omnibus and linked-story series, then the themed modern anthology

subs.label: Serial Drama Traditions
subs.axis: Axis: by the named national or regional long-form serial tradition, Latin American telenovela first, then the Anglo-European soap opera, the Turkish dizi, South Asian serials, the Arabic musalsal, the Philippine teleserye last.

leaves.label: Telenovela
leaves.defn: A closed-ended Latin American (or Latin-modelled) melodrama serial of one central love story told over months of daily episodes (Los ricos también lloran, María la del Barrio, Yo soy Betty, la fea, Rebelde). Brazilian novelas go to B12-2; narco serials go to B12-3.
leaves.see: B12-2 Brazilian Telenovela; B12-3 Narconovela; B12-12 Teleserye
leaves.axis: by production tradition, the Mexican Televisa melodrama first, then South American, Colombian and US Hispanic schools, the youth telenovela, telenovelas made outside Latin America last

leaves.label: Brazilian Telenovela
leaves.defn: A Brazilian novela, typically a Globo prime-time serial with large ensembles and social themes alongside the central romance (Roque Santeiro, Vale Tudo, The Clone). Spanish-language telenovelas go to B12-1.
leaves.see: B12-1 Telenovela

leaves.label: Narconovela
leaves.defn: A telenovela-format serial built around drug traffickers, cartels and the women around them (The Cartel, Pablo Escobar: The Drug Lord, La Reina del Sur). A narco crime series made in a non-telenovela format goes to B7.
leaves.see: B12-1 Telenovela; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Soap Opera
leaves.defn: An open-ended continuing drama broadcast daily or several times a week, with interwoven storylines in a fixed community that can run for decades (Coronation Street, Days of Our Lives, Neighbours, Gute Zeiten, schlechte Zeiten). A weekly prime-time serial of glamour and wealth goes to B12-5.
leaves.aliases: continuing drama; daytime soap; daily soap
leaves.see: B12-5 Prime-Time Soap Opera; B12-7 Indian Television Soap Opera
leaves.axis: by broadcasting tradition: American daytime soaps first, British and Irish continuing drama, Australian and New Zealand soaps, European daily soaps last

leaves.label: Prime-Time Soap Opera
leaves.defn: A weekly evening serial of wealth, glamour, family feuds and revenge, with cliffhangers in place of closure (Dallas, Dynasty, Melrose Place, Desperate Housewives). A daily continuing soap goes to B12-4.
leaves.see: B12-4 Soap Opera; B1-3 Family Drama

leaves.label: Dizi
leaves.defn: A Turkish television serial, typically of long weekly episodes, from the romance melodrama to Ottoman epics (What is Fatmagul's Fault?, Ezel, Erkenci Kuş, The Magnificent Century). A Turkish streaming miniseries outside the broadcast form goes to its genre leaf in B1.
leaves.see: B12-11 Musalsal; B1-19 Historical Drama
leaves.axis: by dizi genre: the melodrama first, the romantic-comedy dizi, crime, revenge and action dizi, family dizi, teen dizi, the Ottoman historical dizi last

leaves.label: Indian Television Soap Opera
leaves.defn: A Hindi (or other Indian-language) daily serial of joint-family conflict, marriage and the saas-bahu (mother-in-law and daughter-in-law) axis (Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai, Anupamaa). Mythological serials go to B12-8.
leaves.see: B12-8 Mythological Serial; B12-9 Pakistani Drama

leaves.label: Mythological Serial
leaves.defn: An Indian television serial retelling Hindu epics and Puranic stories of gods and heroes (Ramayan, Mahabharat, Devon Ke Dev...Mahadev). Biblical and Islamic epics go to B1-19.
leaves.see: B12-7 Indian Television Soap Opera; B1-19 Historical Drama

leaves.label: Pakistani Drama
leaves.defn: A Pakistani Urdu drama serial, typically a closed 20–30 episode story of love, marriage and family duty (Humsafar, Zindagi Gulzar Hai, Meray Paas Tum Ho). Indian daily soaps go to B12-7.
leaves.see: B12-7 Indian Television Soap Opera

leaves.label: Sri Lankan Teledrama
leaves.defn: A Sinhala-language teledrama, the daily or weekly serial of Sri Lankan television (Deweni Inima, Koombiyo). Kept small as the attested national tradition.
leaves.see: B12-7 Indian Television Soap Opera

leaves.label: Musalsal
leaves.defn: An Arabic television serial, classically a 30-episode drama made for the Ramadan season (Bab Al-Hara, Omar, Al Hayba, Raafat Al Haggan). Turkish serials go to B12-6.
leaves.see: B12-6 Dizi; B1-19 Historical Drama
leaves.axis: by musalsal genre: the historical and religious epic first, the social and family serial, crime, spy and thriller serials last

leaves.label: Teleserye
leaves.defn: A Philippine prime-time television serial in the telenovela mould, from romance to fantasy (Marimar, The Promise (Pangako Sa 'Yo), On the Wings of Love). Latin American telenovelas go to B12-1.
leaves.see: B12-1 Telenovela; B1-9 Romantic Drama
